rationales: Metallic bonds form between metal atoms, not two non-metals.
Ionic bonds usually form through electron transfer between a metal and a non-metal.
Covalent bonds form when non-metals share electrons.
Coordinate covalent bonds involve a shared pair donated by one atom and are not the expected general bond between two non-metals.
